1What You Will Learn

  • Explain how notice, choice, the lawful basis and the limits on purpose apply to AI
  • Explain data minimization and privacy by design for AI
  • Explain the controller's duties: assessments, processors, transfers, rights, automated decisions, breaches and records
  • Explain the rules for sensitive and special-category data, including biometrics

2II.A.1: Explain how notice, choice, the lawful basis and the purpose-limitation principle apply to AI

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Understand, so the depth is Understand. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Running case

An Applicant Asks What Helios Holds

  • An EU applicant to the hiring tool writes to Helios: what do you hold about me, and how was I scored?
  • The tool also analyzes a video interview; Veridex hosts the data in the United States
  • Jonas Weber, Head of Legal and Privacy, must answer within the legal deadline
  • You will see which privacy duties are in play and who carries them

Why Privacy Law Reaches AI Beyond the BoK

  • Personal data is any information relating to an identified or identifiable person (General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR, Article 4(1)); processing is any operation on it (Article 4(2))
  • It appears in training data, in inputs and prompts, in outputs and in inferences about people
  • Profiling is automated evaluation of personal aspects such as performance, preferences or behavior (Article 4(4))
  • The controller decides purposes and means; the processor acts on its behalf (Articles 4(7) and 4(8))
  • US state privacy laws, such as Colorado's, use the same ideas: controllers, processors, and rights over profiling

Exam tip: If data relate to an identifiable person at any stage, privacy law applies, even to a model's output.

Transparency and Notice for AI Beyond the BoK

Question What the GDPR asks
Principle process lawfully, fairly and transparently (Article 5(1))
How concise, intelligible, easy to find, clear and plain language (Article 12(1))
When at collection (Article 13); when data come from elsewhere, within the set time (Article 14)
What who the controller is, purposes and legal basis, recipients, transfers, rights
AI-specific the existence of automated decision-making, including profiling, and meaningful information about the logic involved (Article 13(2)(f))
  • Notice for AI must say that AI is used, for what, and with what effect on the person
  • A generic privacy policy line is not enough for a hiring or credit decision

Exam tip: Transparency about AI is part of privacy notice, not only an AI-law duty.

Choice, Consent and the Lawful Basis Beyond the BoK [Verify live]

Basis (Article 6(1)) AI example
Consent (a) an opt-in to have a chat used to improve a model
Contract (b) processing an application the applicant asked for
Legal obligation (c) keeping records the law requires
Vital interests (d) rare in AI; an emergency
Public task (e) a public body's benefit-eligibility model
Legitimate interests (f) fraud detection, product security, sometimes model training, after a balancing test
  • Consent must be freely given, specific, informed and unambiguous; it is weak where there is a power imbalance, as in employment
  • No basis is ranked above another; the controller picks the right one and documents it
  • Legitimate interests need a three-step test: a real interest, necessity, and balancing against people's rights (European Data Protection Board, EDPB, Opinion 28/2024)
  • As of 27 October 2026: proposed GDPR changes for AI training (a new Article 88c) were not confirmed as adopted

Exam tip: Consent is not always the basis; the question usually asks which basis fits the facts.

Purpose Limitation and Reuse of Data

  • Data must be collected for specified, explicit and legitimate purposes and not used in an incompatible way (Article 5(1)(b))
  • To judge compatibility, weigh five factors (Article 6(4)): link between purposes, context, nature of the data, consequences for people, safeguards
  • If the new purpose is not compatible, it needs its own basis, such as consent, or it should not proceed
  • Helios: application data collected to process a job application are not automatically fit to train a screening model

Exam tip: For reuse, ask first whether the new purpose is compatible with the original one.

What the Exam Asks: Notice, Choice, Basis, Purpose

  • Notice must be specific to the use: it names AI, the purpose and the effect
  • Consent is one basis of six, and is often the wrong one in employment
  • A basis is needed for each purpose, including training and reuse
  • Purpose limitation blocks silent reuse; a compatibility check or new basis is required
  • Legitimate interests is not a default: it needs a balancing test and safeguards
  • Penalties: breaches of the principles, lawful basis and rights can be fined up to EUR 20 million or 4% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher (Article 83(5))

Exam tip: If a question lacks a basis for training, the answer is to establish one before using the data.

3II.A.2: Explain how minimizing the data collected, and privacy by design, apply to AI

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Understand, so the depth is Understand. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Data Minimization in AI Systems

  • Data must be adequate, relevant and limited to what is necessary for the purposes (Article 5(1)(c))
  • Also accurate (Article 5(1)(d)) and kept no longer than necessary (Article 5(1)(e))
  • For AI this means: choose features for the purpose, drop what the model does not need, set retention limits for training sets
  • The EDPB asks, for legitimate-interest training, whether there is a less intrusive way and whether the amount of data is proportionate
  • More data for a better model is not a legal defense

Exam tip: Minimization asks for the least data that does the job, not the most data that might help.

Privacy by Design and by Default Beyond the BoK

  • By design (Article 25(1)): build measures, such as pseudonymization, into the system from the start
  • By default (Article 25(2)): only the data needed for each purpose, in the amount, extent, storage period and accessibility
  • Pseudonymization: replace identifiers; extra information is kept apart
  • Differential privacy: add noise so no single person can be singled out
  • Federated learning: train where the data live, share model updates, not the data
  • Synthetic data: artificial data that mimic patterns of real data

Exam tip: Privacy by default is the setting at the start: the narrowest sharing and shortest retention unless the person chooses otherwise.

The Tension: Data-Hungry Models and Minimization

  • Teams want more data, kept longer, from more sources
  • The law asks for the necessary amount, for the purpose, for as long as needed
  • Resolve it with a defined purpose, curated data, privacy-enhancing techniques, and retention limits
  • Document the necessity reasoning; regulators ask for it

Exam tip: The answer to the tension is neither more data nor no AI: it is purpose, curation and technique, with a record.

4II.A.3: Explain how a data controller's duties apply to AI

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Understand, so the depth is Understand. The course has 2 practice questions on this indicator.

Controller, Processor and Joint Controller in AI Beyond the BoK

  • The controller decides purposes and means; the processor acts on its documented instructions (Articles 4(7), 4(8))
  • Joint controllers decide together and must set out who does what; people may exercise rights against each (Article 26)
  • Helios is the controller of applicant data; Veridex screens on its instructions, so it is a processor
  • If Veridex uses the data to improve its own model, it decides a purpose of its own and may become a controller or joint controller
  • Corvid Labs is a processor for chats sent through its interface, on the same test

Exam tip: The label follows who decides purposes and means, not the contract title.

Impact Assessments: DPIA and Its Relatives Beyond the BoK

  • A data protection impact assessment (DPIA) is required before processing that is likely to result in a high risk to people (Article 35(1))
  • Named cases include systematic, extensive evaluation based on automated processing (profiling) leading to significant decisions, and large-scale special-category data (Article 35(3))
  • Minimum content: description and purposes, necessity and proportionality, risks, measures (Article 35(7)); seek the data protection officer's advice (Article 35(2))
  • US: Colorado requires a documented data protection assessment for profiling with defined risks and for sensitive data
  • A DPIA feeds the AI impact assessments of modules 8 and 12

Exam tip: A hiring tool that scores people is a textbook DPIA case: profiling with significant effects.

Third-Party Processors and Sub-Processors

Rule (Article 28) What it means for AI vendors
Sufficient guarantees choose processors that can meet the GDPR; assess them
Binding contract processing only on documented instructions; confidentiality; security; help with rights and assessments; delete or return data; audit information
Sub-processors none without the controller's written authorization; same duties passed down; the first processor stays fully liable
  • In AI supply chains, a model provider or cloud host is often a sub-processor
  • Ask for the list of sub-processors, and bar use of your data to train the vendor's own models without your approval

Exam tip: A processor contract is mandatory, and the vendor cannot add sub-processors without the controller's authorization.

Cross-Border Transfers Beyond the BoK [Verify live]

  • Chapter V governs transfers (Articles 44 to 49); breaches fall in the higher fine tier
  • Adequacy decision (Article 45): the Commission finds a country, territory or sector adequate; no further authorization is needed
  • Otherwise appropriate safeguards (Article 46): standard data protection clauses, binding corporate rules, an approved code of conduct or certification, with enforceable rights and remedies
  • AI cases: training or inference in another region, a hosted model interface abroad, and support staff with remote access
  • As of 27 October 2026: adequacy decisions, such as the EU-US Data Privacy Framework for certified US companies, can be challenged; check the current list

Exam tip: Remote access from a third country is a transfer too; look for the mechanism, not only the server location.

Data Subject Rights Applied to AI Beyond the BoK

Right Article The AI angle
Access 15 a copy of the data; for automated decisions, meaningful information about the logic involved and the consequences
Rectification 16 fix wrong data; wrong inputs mean wrong outputs
Erasure 17 grounds include data no longer needed, withdrawn consent, unlawful processing
Portability 20 data the person provided, under consent or contract, by automated means
Objection 21 to processing based on public task or legitimate interests, including profiling
  • Answer within one month, extendable by two further months where needed (Article 12(3))
  • Erasure from a trained model is hard: prevent it by keeping personal data out of training where possible, and document how requests are handled

Exam tip: Match the right to the request: copy is access, fix is rectification, stop is objection or erasure, move is portability.

Automated Decision-Making: Article 22 and the SCHUFA Ruling Beyond the BoK [Dates]

  • Article 22(1): a right not to be subject to a decision based solely on automated processing, including profiling, with legal or similarly significant effects
  • Exceptions (Article 22(2)): necessary for a contract, authorized by law with safeguards, or based on explicit consent
  • Safeguards (Article 22(3)): at least human intervention, the chance to express a view and to contest the decision
  • Special-category data (Article 22(4)) only with explicit consent or substantial public interest, plus safeguards
  • CJEU, 7 December 2023 (SCHUFA, C-634/21): an automated credit score can itself be a decision where a third party draws strongly on it

Exam tip: A rubber-stamp human review does not turn a solely automated decision into a human one.

Incidents, Breach Notification and Records

  • A processor tells the controller without undue delay (Article 33(2))
  • The controller notifies the authority without undue delay and where feasible within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk (Article 33(1))
  • If risk is high, inform the people without undue delay; not needed if the data were protected, such as by encryption (Article 34)
  • Document every breach, with facts, effects and remedial action (Article 33(5))
  • Record keeping: a record of processing activities (Article 30), with purposes, data, recipients, transfers, retention and security; small organizations are exempt only in limited cases

Exam tip: The 72 hours run from becoming aware, and a late notice must give its reasons.

5II.A.4: Explain the rules for sensitive data and biometrics in AI

Exam angle

The BoK verb is Understand, so the depth is Understand. The course has 1 practice question on this indicator.

Sensitive and Special-Category Data Beyond the BoK

Special categories (Article 9(1)) Examples in AI
Racial or ethnic origin; political opinions; religious or philosophical beliefs; trade union membership a model inferring beliefs from posts
Genetic data; biometric data for unique identification face matching; voiceprints
Data concerning health; sex life or sexual orientation health inferred from a video interview
  • Processing is prohibited unless an exception applies, such as explicit consent, employment law obligations, substantial public interest or legal claims (Article 9(2))
  • Data that reveal a sensitive characteristic can be special-category data even when inferred, and proxies can do the same
  • Solely automated decisions on special categories need explicit consent or substantial public interest (Article 22(4))
  • US laws define sensitive data differently; Colorado requires an assessment for sensitive-data processing

Exam tip: The test is what the data reveal: an inferred health condition is sensitive even if nobody supplied it.

Biometrics, Children and Other High-Risk Data Beyond the BoK

  • Biometric data result from technical processing of physical, physiological or behavioral traits and allow or confirm unique identification (Article 4(14)); used to identify, they are special-category data
  • Illinois BIPA (Biometric Information Privacy Act): informed written release before collection, a published retention and destruction policy, and damages of USD 1,000 or USD 5,000 per violation type (secondary sources)
  • Children: where consent is the basis for online services, the age is 16, which Member States may lower to 13 (Article 8)
  • AI-specific law adds rules for some biometric uses (module 6)

Exam tip: Biometric data are sensitive when used to identify a person; a face scan for unlocking or matching is the typical case.

6Exam Q&A

6.1 Practice questions (one best answer, or select exactly the number the question asks for)

S1Helios wants to use past applicants' data to train a better screening model. The data were collected only to process each application. Under the GDPR, which question should be answered first?

  • AWhether the vendor's marketing material says that the applicant data are fully anonymized
  • BWhether training is compatible with the purpose of collection, and which lawful basis supports it
  • CWhether the training data can be moved to a lower-cost cloud region without a contract change
  • DWhether the applicants have received an annual reminder email about the company's recruiting policy
Show the answer

Answer: B. Reusing data for a new purpose requires a compatibility check against the original purpose, or a new lawful basis, and the controller must document it. Vendor claims, hosting costs and reminder emails do not answer that question.

S2Which TWO measures best serve data minimization and privacy by design in a screening model? (Select TWO.)

  • ARemove input fields that are not needed for the stated purpose of the model
  • BCollect the broadest set of applicant data points in case it improves accuracy later
  • CPseudonymize the training data and limit who can access it and for how long
  • DKeep the application data for as long as models might need to be retrained in the future
  • EPublish the full training dataset online to demonstrate openness to the public
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Minimization means limiting data to what the purpose needs, and design measures such as pseudonymization and access and retention limits support it. Collecting everything, keeping data indefinitely and publishing the dataset all work against the principle.

S3Helios plans to send EU applicants' data to Veridex's servers in the United States. Which statement is correct?

  • ANo transfer mechanism is needed, because Veridex acts as a processor for Helios
  • BA note in the privacy notice is enough, because applicants have not objected to the transfer
  • CA transfer mechanism is needed only if the data contain special categories of personal data
  • DA transfer mechanism is needed, such as an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards
Show the answer

Answer: D. A transfer to a third country needs an adequacy decision or appropriate safeguards, such as standard data protection clauses, whether the recipient is a controller or a processor. The data type does not decide whether a mechanism is needed, and a notice alone is not one.

S4An EU job applicant is rejected automatically by a score, with no human review. The applicant asks the company for a copy of their data, a correction of a wrong employment date, and an explanation of how the score was reached. Which THREE rights are engaged? (Select THREE.)

  • AThe right to erasure of the data held in the application file
  • BThe right of access, including a copy of the personal data
  • CThe right to portability of the application data to another employer
  • DThe right to rectification of the inaccurate employment date
  • EThe right to meaningful information about the logic of the automated decision
Show the answer

Answer: B, D, E. The applicant asks for a copy (access), a fix (rectification) and an explanation of an automated decision (meaningful information about the logic involved). Nothing in the request asks for erasure or for the data to be moved to another controller.

S5A model infers an applicant's health condition from a video interview and uses it in scoring. How does the GDPR treat the inferred information?

  • AIt is not personal data, because the applicant did not provide it to the company
  • BIt is ordinary personal data, because an inference is a statistical guess
  • CIt is special-category data if it reveals health, so Article 9 conditions apply
  • DIt may be used, because legitimate interests cover scoring decisions
Show the answer

Answer: C. Data that reveal a sensitive characteristic, such as health, fall under the special categories even when they are inferred, so a prohibition applies unless an Article 9 exception is met. An inference about a person is still personal data, and legitimate interests alone do not lift the prohibition.

7Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Notice, basis, purpose tell people about AI use; pick and document a lawful basis; check compatibility before reuse
Minimization and design the least data, built in from the start and by default; privacy-enhancing techniques
Controller duties assess (DPIA), contract processors, secure transfers, answer rights, control automated decisions, notify breaches, keep records
Sensitive data prohibited unless an exception applies; what data reveal counts; biometrics, children and inferences need extra care
Roles controller, processor and joint controller follow who decides purposes and means
